question: What did the screenwriter William Goldman mean by 'Nobody knows anything'?
answer: That in Hollywood not one person knows for certain which film will succeed. Goldman called it the single most important fact about the film business: studio heads, stars and writers are all guessing, which is why proven formulas flop and turned-down scripts become hits.
move: When experts can't predict success, beware anyone who claims they can.
simply: Even the bosses of Hollywood can't tell which films will be hits. They're guessing, like everyone else.
why: The same holds for books, apps and start-ups. Knowing that success is hard to predict makes failure less personal and luck easier to see.
